title: Selecting a complete sample of blazars in sub-millimetre catalogues
question: How to efficiently select a complete sample of blazars in sub-millimetre catalogues (specifically H-ATLAS) and determine their number counts at 500 μm.

what.value: 5th edition of the Multifrequency Catalogue of Blazars (BZCAT)

evidence.quote: To define improved selection criteria we first cross-matched the H-ATLAS catalogues with the latest (5th) edition of the BZCAT (cite: Massaro2015b)

what.value: 1.4 GHz peak flux densities from FIRST and NVSS catalogues

evidence.quote: For the equatorial and NGP fields we adopted the $1.4\,$GHz peak flux densities from the FIRST catalogue. For the SGP field, not covered by the FIRST survey, we used those from the NRAO VLA Sky Survey (cite: Condon1998).

The Australia Telescope 20 GHz (cite: mm2008MNRAS384; mm2011MNRAS412; murphy2010MNRAS402) survey covered the whole Southern sky at 20 GHz above a typical flux density limit of 40 mJy, with follow-up at 5.5 and 9.0 GHz.

The *Planck* ATCA Co-eval Observations (cite: mm2011MNRAS415; bonavera2011MNRAS416; bonaldi2013MNRAS428; galluzzi2017MNRAS465; Galluzzi2018) catalogue was built by following up with the ATCA a sample of AT20G sources

what.value: WISE-selected blazar candidate catalogues WIBRaLS2 and KDEBLLACS

evidence.quote: we have cross-matched H-ATLAS sources brighter than our flux-density threshold ($S_{500\mu{\rm m}}=35\,$mJy) with the two catalogues of radio-loud candidate blazars selected by (cite: DAbrusco2019) on the basis of WISE colours.

what.value: Blazar Radio and Optical Survey (BROS) catalogue

evidence.quote: (cite: Itoh2020) built a new catalogue of blazar candidates, named Blazar Radio and Optical Survey (BROS).
Table 4 shows the results of a cross-match of H-ATLAS sources with the 4FGL catalogue using as search radius the 95% confidence semi-major axis of the 4FGL error ellipse.

what.value: Blazar number count estimates from ALMA calibrator data

evidence.loc: Number counts of sub-mm selected Blazars
evidence.quote: Our counts are in reasonably good agreement with, although somewhat lower than the estimate obtained by (cite: Bonato2019) at 467 GHz

recipe.goal: Select initial known blazars and define sub-mm/radio colour selection criteria
recipe.method: Cross-match H-ATLAS catalogues with BZCAT (5th edition) and 1.4 GHz radio surveys (FIRST and NVSS), then compute SPIRE and 1.4 GHz flux density ratios to define selection boundaries.
key_parameters: S_500um > 35 mJy; 0.5 < S_250um/S_350um < 1.2; 0.4 < S_350um/S_500um < 1.2; S_500um/S_1.4GHz < 1.7; search radius = 10 to 15 arcsec

recipe.goal: Follow up candidate blazars in radio and cross-match with radio/mm catalogues to classify genuine blazars
recipe.method: Observe candidates with ATCA and VLA, cross-match with AT20G, PACO, ALMA calibrator catalogue, and NED, and use radio-to-sub-mm colour-colour plots and SEDs to separate synchrotron-dominated blazars from dusty galaxies.

recipe.goal: Estimate synchrotron peak frequencies and derive 500 um blazar number counts
recipe.method: Fit rest-frame SEDs with a parabola in nu*L_nu to find synchrotron peak frequencies, and compute differential and integral number counts at 500 um with Poisson errors.
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 67.37 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 and Omega_m = 0.315
